title: Chapter 14 — Dishwashers
intro: Decibels, rack systems, wash performance, and the installation realities that make or break the sale.

sections.title: Decibels: The Number That Sells Dishwashers
content: Dishwashers are sold on noise. After price, decibel rating is the single most important spec customers ask about — especially in open-concept kitchens where the dishwasher runs while the family is in the living room.
**55+ dBA** — Entry level. You can hear it clearly from the next room. Amana, Hotpoint, budget Frigidaire. Acceptable for rental units and budget buyers. Not for open kitchens.
**48–54 dBA** — Mid-range. Audible but not disruptive. Background conversation level. Most Whirlpool, Maytag, Samsung, LG models. Good enough for most customers.
**44–47 dBA** — Premium quiet. You have to stand next to it to hear it. Bosch 500 Series, KitchenAid, GE Profile. This is the sweet spot for most kitchen renovations.

**38–43 dBA** — Ultra-quiet. Virtually silent. Bosch 800/Benchmark, Miele, Thermador, Cove, JennAir. The customer buying at this level has an open kitchen and demands silence. Floor demonstration tip: run a 44 dBA and a 55 dBA unit simultaneously. The difference is dramatic and sells the upgrade instantly.

sections.title: Tub Material: Plastic vs Stainless
content: **Plastic tub.** Found in entry-level dishwashers (Amana, Hotpoint, some Frigidaire). Retains odors, stains from tomato sauce and curry, doesn't conduct heat as well for drying. Lower cost.

**Stainless steel tub.** Standard from mid-tier up. Better heat retention (improves drying), doesn't stain, more durable, more hygienic. Beko uses stainless steel even at entry-level prices — a strong selling point against plastic-tub competitors at the same price.
This is a tangible demo: open a plastic-tub dishwasher and a stainless-tub dishwasher side by side. Let the customer knock on each one. The quality difference is obvious.

sections.title: Rack Systems and Third Racks
content: **Standard two-rack.** Upper and lower racks. Entry and mid-tier. Adequate but limits loading flexibility.

**Third rack.** An additional shallow rack at the top for utensils, small items, and measuring cups. Frees up space in the lower racks. Bosch popularized this. Now available from most brands at mid-tier and above. KitchenAid FreeFlex third rack is adjustable in height.

**Adjustable racks.** Upper rack height adjustment (usually 2–3 positions) accommodates tall items on the bottom rack — wine glasses, pots, tall containers. Some brands offer fold-down tines that create flat loading zones.

**Silverware: basket vs third rack.** Traditional basket sits in the bottom rack. Third rack eliminates the basket, opening up more bottom rack space. Some customers prefer the basket (easier to grab all silverware at once). Neither is wrong — it's personal preference.

sections.title: Drying Technology
content: Drying is where dishwashers differentiate at the premium level.
**Heated dry.** A heating element bakes moisture off the dishes. Uses more energy. Can damage some plastics. Standard on most dishwashers.

**Condensation dry.** The final hot rinse creates steam; stainless steel walls are cooler, so moisture condenses on the walls and drains away. Used by Bosch and European brands. Works well on ceramics and glass; plastics stay wet because they don't retain heat.
**AutoAir (Bosch 500).** The door pops open automatically at the end of the cycle to release steam. Simple and effective. No energy cost.

**CrystalDry (Bosch 800/Benchmark).** Uses zeolite minerals that absorb moisture and convert it to heat. Dries everything — including plastics. Bosch's premium drying technology and a genuine differentiator.
**Fan dry.** An internal fan circulates air to speed drying. Common in KitchenAid and Whirlpool premium models.

The demo: show the customer a CrystalDry Bosch dishwasher and point out the zeolite container. Explain that it dries plastics — something no heated-dry dishwasher does well. This converts Bosch sales.

sections.title: Installation and Selling
content: **Standard size.** 24" wide, built into a cabinet opening. Universal fit. 99% of dishwashers are this size.
**18" compact.** For small kitchens, condo galleys, and wet bars. Limited selection. Bosch and Miele offer 18" models.
**Panel-ready.** The front accepts a custom cabinet panel so the dishwasher disappears into the cabinetry. Premium and luxury. Bosch Benchmark, Miele, Cove, JennAir, Thermador.
**ADA-compliant.** Shorter height for accessible installations. Most brands offer ADA variants.
**Dishwasher add-ons.** Stainless steel installation kits, power cords (many premium dishwashers don't include one), water supply lines. These are margin items.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
content: Run every dishwasher on your floor. Listen to the noise levels. Open every door and pull out every rack. Know which have third racks, which dry plastics, and which are panel-ready. When a customer says 'I just need a dishwasher,' your first question is: 'How open is your kitchen?' That answer determines whether noise matters, and noise determines the price range.
